A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 34-page study, including Appendices A–G. Text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison; differences are confined to front matter and negligible typesetting shifts.

before.justification: v2 reports original real-world robot experiments on four manipulation tasks, including scaling curves, model comparisons and task success rates (Sections 4–6; Appendix G).

after.justification: v3 retains the original robot experiments and their results, including scaling curves, model comparisons and success rates across four tasks (Sections 4–6; Appendix G).

M1.justification: Both retain the same DINOv2-based Diffusion Policy, DDIM inference, temporal ensemble, task-specific observation horizons and recommended data collection strategy (Sections 3 and 4.3; Appendix C).

E1.justification: Both evaluate Pour Water, Mouse Arrangement, Fold Towels and Unplug Charger with the same object, environment and joint generalization scenarios. Training and testing coverage in Appendix A is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same comparisons involving learning from scratch, frozen DINOv2, LoRA and full fine-tuning, alongside the same visual-encoder and U-Net sizes.

E3.justification: Data subsets, training schedules, scoring and success criteria, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Appendices C–E retain the same settings and blind testing workflow.

E4.justification: The diversity and demonstration-count analyses, multiple-objects-per-environment experiment, and model ablations are retained unchanged. The metric comparison in Appendix E.1 and supplementary scaling analyses in G.1–G.2 also match.

E5.justification: Both report the same 95% confidence intervals for scaling results and standard deviations across eight unseen environments in Table 1. No trial-count, seed or uncertainty-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout. Table 1 retains success rates of 85.0%, 92.5%, 87.5% and 90.0% for the four tasks; model comparisons and Appendix G's raw scores and per-environment results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The environment/object/demonstration formulation, optimality-gap definition, power-law fitting equations and irreducible-error caveat are unchanged (Sections 3 and 4.2).

C1.justification: Both retain the same claims about approximate power-law scaling with environment/object diversity, diminishing returns from additional demonstrations, and efficient collection enabling roughly 90% task success.

C2.justification: Interpretations of diversity, model scaling and MSE reliability are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations, and Appendix E.2 preserves the restriction against comparing results across separate evaluation batches.

D1.justification: Appendices B, C and F retain the same collection guidance, hyperparameters, training compute and hardware details. The project link and stated release of code, data and models are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B.1 and the bibliography contain the same cited works and research positioning, including comparisons with OXE, UMI, RUMs and compositional-generalization research.

P1.justification: The first two authors change from Fanqi Lin followed by Yingdong Hu to Yingdong Hu followed by Fanqi Lin, retaining equal-contribution markings. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; prose and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–23 and Tables 1–12 retain the same content, captions, axes, legends, structures and placement. Negligible text-position shifts do not constitute a layout revision.

improvement.justification: v3 changes author order and arXiv front matter while retaining the scientific text, experimental evidence, limitations and reproducibility information, including all appendices. These edits establish no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
